name: The Class for Representing a TV (Case 2)
description: Construct a class that represents a TV. The class should contain data that represents the TV's state (power on or off, current volume level). The state of the TV could be accessed or changed only through the getter and setter methods. The class should also include methods to change the state of the TV (turn on/off, change volume level). Assume that the volume level is an integer and ranges from 1 to 7 (both inclusive).

commentList: We define the class named TV2 to represent a TV.

3.content: #Step 1.1: Initialize the state of the TV

We do this by defining an __init__ method, which is run automatically by Python each time an instance is created. The argument (named self) is passed in automatically by the interpreter when the method is invoked on an instance of the class.

Note that Python automatically fills the first argument in with the instance object that is the implied subject of the method call. Therefore, when this method is invoked on an instance of the class, no parameter must be passed to the method.

This statement sets the on/off state of the TV to False because, by default, the TV is off.
self is the instance of the class and self.__on shows whether the TV is on. The self.__on is True when the TV is on, and False otherwise. We start the attribute name by two underscore (self.__on) to prevent accessing the attribute directly from outside of the class.

12.content: #Step 1.3: Define the methods to change the volume level of the TV

commentList: This method set the current volume level of the TV to the given volume level (new_volume_level) that is specified as the method's parameter. The first argument (named self) is passed in automatically by the interpreter when the method is invoked on an instance of the class.

14.content: if self.__on and new_volume_level >= 1 and new_volume_level <= 7 :
commentList: We need to perform a test to check whether the conditions for changing the current volume level of the TV to the given volume level exist. The current volume level of the TV could be set to the given volume level only when the TV is on and the given volume level is within the valid volume level range. A valid range for the TV volume level is from 1 to 7 (both inclusive).

The if statement tests whether the TV is on and the given volume level is greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to 7. If the TV is on and the given volume level is greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to 7, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
Note that the and operator yields the result True if both conditions are True.

This statement sets the current volume level of the TV to the given value (new_volume_level).
